evaluations.title: Composed Context-Effect Pilot with Artifact-Preserving Controls
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Construct three candidate logit tables and pre-register the composed context-effect table as the primary target. The experiment tests whether context-induced logit perturbations across shared probes occupy a lower-dimensional subspace than controls that preserve probe/token marginals but destroy cross-probe context alignment.

evaluations.title: Candidate Logit Tables: Local, Composed Delta, and Trajectory
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates three candidate logit tables to identify non-trivial low-rank structure: a local prompt-by-token matrix, a composed context-probe delta matrix, and a context-length trajectory matrix. Robustness is verified against token-shuffled controls.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Baseline Marginal Prompt-by-Token Matrix
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Construct a basic prompt-by-token logit table. Evaluate low-rank structure using SVD and softmax KL divergence against a column-shuffled control.

evaluations.title: Landscape of low-rank structure in OLMo-1B logit tables: three tables, marginal-preserving controls
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Foundational measurement to map where nontrivial low-rank structure appears in
OLMo-1B next-token logit tables. We build three tables (simple context-by-token,
composed context+probe blocks, and a context-influence-shift difference table with
a fixed prediction target), measure their spectra/effective rank/rank-r
reconstruction, and contrast each against a per-column-independent-shuffle null
that preserves every column marginal while destroying joint structure. We test a
pre-registered prediction and attribute the dominant component to the unigram prior.

evaluations.title: Baseline Local and Compositional Logit Tables vs. Controls
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a simple prompt-by-token matrix (Table A) and a composed context-by-intervention block matrix (Table B). Compares the singular value spectrum and KL-divergence of rank-k approximations against matched token-shuffled controls to isolate syntactic structure from unigram/bag-of-words artifacts.

evaluations.title: Three-table low-rank survey: naive vs composed vs intervention-difference logit tables
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
A first-principles survey of three logit-table arrangements from OLMo-1B to determine which
shows nontrivial low-rank structure that exceeds matched controls and generalizes to held-out
contexts. We separate architectural rank caps and unigram/marginal nuisance from genuine shared
latent factors using a control hierarchy (column-permutation and token-shuffle) and a held-out
projection test. The novel candidate is an intervention-difference (transfer) table that subtracts
the fragment baseline to isolate how context causally modulates post-fragment predictions.

evaluations.title: Phase 1.1: Robustness Check - Held-Out Transfer & Token Selection Ablation
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the Phase 1 prompt-by-token matrix by checking if the low-rank structure persists across a held-out context split and testing if it depends on the dynamic top-K token selection vs. a fixed subset of frequent tokens.

evaluations.title: Is the context-influence-shift low rank intrinsic? Effective-rank plateau under size scaling (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #4 found that after removing the dominant unigram/scale direction, OLMo-1B
logit tables show control-separated low-rank structure, most cleanly in the
context-influence-shift difference table (T3, r*=2-4 for 70% variance). This
experiment tests whether that low rank is INTRINSIC rather than an artifact of
matrix dimensions, by sweeping the number of contexts N and selected tokens k and
asking whether the recovered rank plateaus while the matched-marginal null keeps
tracking matrix size.

evaluations.title: Crossed Probe Validation for Composed Context-Effect Low Rank
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Validate the positive Eval #1 finding using a stricter crossed hold-out test. The experiment asks whether the composed context-effect table can predict the held-out context by held-out probe-token quadrant, rather than only reconstructing held-out contexts over already-known probe columns.

evaluations.title: Coherence control ladder: does real text yield higher or lower effective rank than matched incoherence controls?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
Experiment 6 surfaced a control reversal: for the prompt-by-token logit table under column-centering,
token-shuffled text appeared MORE low-rank than coherent text on seed 0, while column-permutation was
least low-rank. This experiment rigorously characterizes how the effective dimensionality of the
prompt-by-token logit table depends on input coherence using a matched control ladder
(real, global token-shuffle, within-fragment shuffle, random-token, column-permutation) across multiple
seeds, with SCALE-INVARIANT dimensionality measures plus norm/entropy/cosine diagnostics that separate
true dimensionality from matrix-scale artifacts. Goal: determine the robust ordering and identify which
controls actually distinguish genuine structure from trivial artifacts.

evaluations.title: Low-Rank Structure of Logit Differences Induced by Interventions
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a logit-difference table to isolate the causal effect of interventions on next-token predictions. Evaluates whether the logit updates (Delta logits) induced by natural probes reside in a lower-dimensional subspace than updates induced by token-shuffled probes, effectively controlling for baseline context entropy in KL-divergence calculations.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Context-Probe Concatenation Matrix
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a logit matrix where rows are context prefixes and columns are concatenated probes evaluated for active tokens. Tests if compositional low-rank structure exists beyond bag-of-words using a token-shuffled context control.

evaluations.title: Residualized Crossed Validation of Context-Effect Logit Tables
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the crossed low-rank structure from Eval #9 survives after removing context-specific token effects shared across probes. This distinguishes a richer context-probe low-rank interaction from a simpler additive context-token bias.

evaluations.title: Held-out validation: does the T3 intrinsic steering subspace generalize, and beat the simple-table baseline? (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Pre-registered confirmatory test (locked before running). Eval #8 showed the
context-influence-shift difference table T3_average has intrinsic rank ~5 (real r70
near-flat vs a per-column-shuffle null that grows with matrix size). Here we test
whether the TRAIN-fitted top-5 subspace generalizes to HELD-OUT context fragments
with persistent control separation, and whether this difference-table construction
reaches a target held-out variance at lower rank than the standard simple
context-by-token table (T1) under an identical protocol (independent variable =
table construction).

evaluations.title: Scale-up and spectral-floor validation of the coherence effective-rank ordering
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #10 found, with scale-invariant measures and 5 seeds, that real coherent text produces a HIGHER effective-rank prompt-by-token logit table than incoherence controls (global/within shuffle, random token) but a much LOWER one than the column-permutation floor, with diagnostics (low row cosine, low predictive entropy) ruling out a norm artifact. This experiment tests robustness to matrix size (N in {64,128,192}) and adds a principled spectral reference: a matched-Gaussian / Marchenko-Pastur null whose bulk edge defines a "significant rank" threshold. The headline is the held-out generalization gap (real vs column-permutation), establishing that real text carries genuine low-rank structure that generalizes, distinct from

evaluations.title: Fraction of KL Explained: Balanced Token Union for Logit Differences
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the low-rank compositional structure of logit updates. Fixes the token-selection confound by using a balanced union of top tokens from both natural and corrupted interventions. Shifts the primary probabilistic metric from Absolute KL to Fraction of KL Explained (Relative KL Recovery) to account for the massive difference in baseline distributional shifts.

evaluations.title: Strict Marginal-Preserving Control and Proper Probability KL
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2 revealed that simply comparing natural text to permuted text confounds structural low-rankness with variance scale. This eval introduces a strict column-wise entry-shuffle control that perfectly preserves marginal token variance. It also corrects the KL calculation by explicitly un-centering the reconstructed SVD matrices before applying softmax.

evaluations.title: Post-Residualization Control Robustness for Crossed T3 Low Rank
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the residualized crossed low-rank advantage from Eval #13 survives stricter control ordering and row-strength ablations. The primary control residualizes first, then destroys cross-probe row alignment, avoiding the concern that shuffling before residualization unfairly disrupts context-token baseline estimation.

evaluations.title: Column semantics of the intrinsic steering subspace: rank-slot vs fixed-token-identity columns (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #14 showed the T3 context-influence-shift subspace generalizes across held-out
contexts (H1/H2/H3 passed) but transfers poorly across held-out probes. A candidate
confound is the column definition: T3_average uses probe-rank-SLOT columns (the j-th
top token of each probe) rather than fixed shared TOKEN-IDENTITY columns. This
ablation isolates the column-semantics variable to determine whether the intrinsic
low rank and its context/probe generalization depend on rank-slot vs token-identity
columns. This is the task-required token-selection ablation.

evaluations.title: Context-modulation transfer table: does context influence occupy a low-dim, probe-independent subspace?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
My single-snapshot results (Eval #10, #15) show real next-token logit tables have a small number of
genuine above-noise dimensions that generalize across held-out contexts, while incoherence controls
collapse to a low-dim fallback. This experiment introduces a paired-fragment TRANSFER table that goes
beyond a single snapshot: for many contexts and a shared set of short probe fragments, we measure how
each context MODULATES the post-probe next-token logits. We test whether context modulation occupies a
low-dimensional, probe-INDEPENDENT subspace via a cross-probe held-out transfer test, and whether the
coherence-ladder ordering on this transfer table replicates or flips relative to the single-snapshot table.

evaluations.title: Naturalness Gradient for Residualized Crossed T3 Low-Rank Transfer
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether residualized crossed low-rank transfer is stronger for coherent natural contexts than for increasingly corrupted prefix controls. Each condition uses the same shared-token residualized T3 crossed-validation protocol and its own post-residualization blockwise control.

evaluations.title: Transform ablation on the fixed-token context-influence table: raw vs row-centered vs double-centered (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #19 established the fixed-token-identity context-influence-shift difference table
(B) as the cleanest object: context- and probe-general, intrinsic rank ~2-3. This
task-required ablation isolates the role of the logit TRANSFORM (raw, row-centered,
double-centered) on B's intrinsic rank and its held-out context/probe transfer, to
determine which centering is essential vs incidental before mechanism decoding. We
also fix a metric subtlety from Eval #19 by reporting the real-vs-null gap across the
full rank curve rather than only at rank 5.

evaluations.title: Multi-Seed Replication and Qualitative Grounding of Balanced Delta Matrices
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a robust 3-seed replication of the balanced-token Logit Difference protocol (Fraction of KL Explained). Additionally, extracts the top tokens associated with the first principal component of the natural Delta matrix to qualitatively ground the low-rank update mechanism.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Autoregressive Trajectory Delta Matrix
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the causal logit update applied by contexts at multiple intermediate positions inside a probe. Tests whether natural sequence order induces a structured, low-rank perturbation trajectory compared to token-shuffled contexts.

evaluations.title: Ablation: robustness of the coherence low-rank ordering to centering and token-selection
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My main finding (Evals #10, #15) is that real next-token logit tables show genuine low-rank structure relative to a marginal-preserving column-permutation floor (a small Marchenko-Pastur significant rank that generalizes to held-out contexts), yet appear HIGH-rank relative to incoherence controls that collapse the model to a low-dim fallback. This experiment tests how robust the effective-rank ORDERING and the real-vs-permutation held-out generalization gap are to two key analytic choices the task flags for ablation: the logit transform (raw / row-center / col-center / double-center) and the token-selection rule (top-magnitude / random-subset / frequency-fixed). The goal is to scope exactly which choices the

evaluations.title: Word-Level Naturalness Gradient for Residualized Crossed T3
evaluations.author: Noesis I
evaluations.abstract: Replicate the Eval #21 naturalness-gradient finding using word-level corruptions generated before tokenization. This tests whether natural contexts remain stronger than within-fragment shuffles when the corruption avoids arbitrary token-id permutations and better matches ordinary text-like token boundaries.

evaluations.title: Intrinsic-dimension plateau and unigram decomposition of the fixed-token context-influence table (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Consolidating experiment for the Arkhe line. We test, on the canonical fixed-token
context-influence difference table (established cleanest in Evals #19/#22), whether
its intrinsic dimension is STABLE as the matrix grows (a true low-dimensional
property) versus tracking matrix size (a sampling artifact), and how the structure
decomposes relative to the dominant unigram/scale direction. We track r*(fixed
variance) and the max-over-rank real-vs-per-column-shuffle gap as N and k grow, and
measure the stability of the rank-1 unigram component (its correlation with the
mean-logit profile and its share of variance) across sizes. This is the definitive
test of the intrinsic-dimensionality claim.

evaluations.title: Preregistered fresh-seed confirmation and token-dimension ablation of the control-dependent low-rank finding
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: This is a preregistered confirmation of my main finding (Evals #10, #15, #25) on FRESH seeds not used in any exploratory run, plus the task-required selected-token-dimension (K) ablation. Preregistered predictions (fixed before running): for OLMo-1B row-centered prompt-by-token tables at N=128, (P1) the Marchenko-Pastur significant rank of real text exceeds that of a marginal-preserving column-permutation floor; (P2) a rank-8 subspace fit on training contexts reconstructs held-out contexts with lower relative Frobenius error than the column-permutation floor (positive gap); (P3) mean pairwise row cosine is lower for real than for each incoherence control (the fallback-collapse signature); (P4) entropy effective-rank ordering is incoherent-controls

evaluations.title: Floor-robust pre-registered confirmation of the intrinsic-rank plateau on fresh seeds (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #27 showed the fixed-token context-influence table's effective rank grows far
more slowly than its per-column-shuffle null (real ER-slope ~0.01-0.03 vs null
~0.04-0.09), but the pre-registered largest/smallest r*(70%) RATIO statistic was
degenerate due to an r*=1 floor at the smallest size and thus mis-fired. This
experiment pre-registers a floor-robust statistic (effective-rank slope vs matrix
size, continuous and floor-free) and confirms it on FRESH random seeds, to test the
intrinsic-dimension plateau without the floor artifact and without post-hoc reanalysis.

evaluations.title: Structure-Preserving Control: Circular Row Shift on Trajectory Matrix
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 17 showed that Trajectory Prefix-Length matrices are highly low-rank compared to independent column-entry shuffles. This evaluation stress-tests that result against a strictly stronger 'Circular Row Shift' control. This control randomly shifts each column vertically, perfectly preserving the step-to-step smoothness, total variance, and marginal distribution of every column, while only breaking the cross-token synchronization.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Temporal Coherence Ladder via Independent Position-Wise Delta Matrices
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the temporal emergence of the coherence ladder. Computes independent Trajectory Delta Matrices for each intermediate probe position (m=1..5) to measure how the rank complexity gap between real and token-shuffled text evolves dynamically.

evaluations.title: Held-Out Validation of Balanced Delta Matrix Low-Rank Projections
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the low-dimensional steering subspace identified in the logit-difference (Delta) matrix generalizes to held-out contexts. Fits the SVD on a training set of 64 contexts and measures the Fraction of KL Explained when projecting the Delta updates of 16 held-out contexts into this learned basis.

evaluations.title: Token Union Size Ablation for Balanced Delta Matrices
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an ablation study on the balanced token union size (k) to ensure the Fraction of KL Explained advantage of natural Delta matrices over corrupted matrices is not an artifact of small token subsets. Evaluates k=10, k=20, and k=30 balanced token union sizes.

evaluations.title: Geometry and content of the genuine low-rank logit subspace: cross-seed stability and a shared context code
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My published finding (Archive #2) is that the row-centered prompt-by-token OLMo-1B logit table has ~4-7 Marchenko-Pastur-significant, held-out-generalizing dimensions relative to a marginal-preserving floor. This experiment asks WHAT those dimensions are: (1) are the token-axis significant subspaces STABLE across independent text seeds (principal-angle overlap above a marginal-preserving and a matched-Gaussian null), and does stability survive removing the token-frequency direction; (2) do contexts occupy the SAME low-dim coordinates whether described by their raw next-token preferences (snapshot table) or by how they MODULATE post-probe predictions (transfer table) — a shared context code, tested by within-seed principal angles between the two left-singular subspaces; (3)

evaluations.title: Does intrinsic dimension grow with context length? Length-resolved ER-slope scaling of the context-influence table (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Within my approved intrinsic-dimension-scaling lane, this experiment asks whether the
intrinsic dimension of the context-influence difference table DEPENDS ON CONTEXT LENGTH.
Longer contexts carry more information and might steer predictions along more directions
(intrinsic dimension grows with length) or might still collapse to a fixed low-
dimensional steering subspace (length-invariant). We measure the effective-rank-slope
ratio (real vs per-column-shuffle null) and the intrinsic dimension separately for
contexts binned by token length, with the unigram decomposition tracked per bin.

evaluations.title: Does intrinsic dimension scale with probe-set size? Probe-averaging concentration test for the fixed-token context-influence table (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Second scaling axis in the intrinsic-dimension lane. We hold context length fixed and vary the NUMBER of probe fragments averaged in the fixed-token T3 context-influence difference table. We test whether the effective-rank-vs-matrix-size plateau persists across probe-set sizes, and we measure the descriptive trend of intrinsic dimension as more probes are averaged. The mechanistic prediction (distinct from the context-length axis, which mildly increased intrinsic dim) is that averaging more probes suppresses probe-specific noise and CONCENTRATES the table onto its shared context-effect subspace, so intrinsic dimension should decrease or stabilize with probe count.

evaluations.title: Graded fallback collapse: is incoherence-driven dimensionality loss smooth and mediated by predictive entropy?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract:
My published work (Archive #2) showed incoherent inputs collapse OLMo-1B into a low-dimensional,
high-entropy fallback, flipping the apparent low-rank verdict. This experiment characterizes the COLLAPSE
as a function of input naturalness along a finely spaced corruption gradient, and tests whether the loss
of effective dimensionality is SMOOTH or threshold-like and whether it is statistically MEDIATED by
per-context predictive entropy. We measure scale-invariant effective rank, MP significant rank, mean
pairwise row cosine, and predictive entropy across a graded ladder, and perform a mediation analysis
(does controlling for predictive entropy remove the naturalness-to-dimensionality relationship?).

evaluations.title: Subspace Alignment: Trajectory Updates Predict Context-Probe Modulation
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests a unified geometric theory: that the low-dimensional subspace in which a context's state evolves during sequential reading (the Trajectory matrix) is perfectly aligned with the subspace it uses to modulate future predictions (the Composed ContextxProbe matrix). We extract context factors from prefix-reading trajectories and use them in a bilinear bridge to zero-shot predict fully held-out context-probe interactions.

evaluations.title: Autoregressive Trajectory Delta Matrices: Subspace Overlap Across Sequential Updates
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Delta matrix framework to multi-step autoregressive trajectories. Evaluates whether the low-rank compositional update subspace rotates smoothly (high adjacent-step overlap) for natural language compared to the orthogonal thrashing of syntax-destroyed gibberish. Uses a globally fixed balanced token subset across 4 trajectory steps to ensure comparable vector spaces.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.1: Temporal Coherence Ladder - Balanced Token Union and Fractional KL
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the token-selection rule for the Temporal Coherence Ladder (Eval 31) using a Balanced Token Union (Archive #4) to normalize baseline entropy confounds, verifying the dynamic peak at position m=2.

evaluations.title: Why does probe-averaging concentrate intrinsic dimension? Per-probe subspace alignment vs variance-averaging mechanism (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #36 showed that averaging more probes DECREASES the intrinsic dimension of the fixed-token context-influence table, opposite to the context-length axis. This experiment discriminates the mechanism: is the concentration (M1) denoising onto a SHARED low-dimensional context-effect subspace already present in each single-probe table, or (M2) cancellation of probe-specific directions across misaligned subspaces, or (M3) a trivial statistical variance-averaging artifact? We measure per-probe single-table intrinsic dimension, cross-probe principal-angle subspace alignment, and a variance-matched control that isolates pure averaging from genuine cross-probe structure.

evaluations.title: Exp C: Preregistered out-of-sample confirmation of variant-dependent entropy-mediation of fallback-collapse
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #37 found a dissociation in how incoherence-driven dimensionality collapse relates to entropy: random_token corruption appeared fully entropy-mediated (partial correlation of naturalness with effective rank, controlling entropy, ~0; CI included 0), whereas within_shuffle corruption retained a substantial DIRECT coherence channel beyond entropy (partial r~0.67). This experiment tests whether that dissociation replicates out-of-sample on fresh seeds and is robust across table size N, selected-token dimension K, and token-selection rule. The independent variable is corruption family (within_shuffle vs random_token) and the preregistered claim is about the SIGN and ordering of the entropy-controlled direct channel, not its exact magnitude.

evaluations.title: Terminal Subspace Projection: Geometric Constraints on Autoregressive Trajectories
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether intermediate autoregressive logit updates are bounded by the low-dimensional geometry of the final composed meaning. Calculates the Terminal Subspace (top principal components of the total 4-token Delta update) and measures the fraction of variance (Relative Frobenius Error) of intermediate step updates that is captured by projection onto this terminal basis, comparing natural versus syntax-destroyed trajectories across 3 seeds.

evaluations.title: Does probe-averaging concentration survive unigram-profile removal? Deflated variance-matched control re-comparison (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #41 found the probe-averaging intrinsic-dimension concentration is reproduced (over-reproduced) by a variance-matched shuffle-averaging control, selecting M3 (trivial variance-averaging) under the pre-registered rule. But the control preserves the per-column unigram profile and may over-collapse toward that single direction. This experiment removes the unigram/column-profile component in BOTH the real averaged table and the variance-matched control before comparing intrinsic dimension, to test whether any genuine shared cross-probe concentration survives once the dominant unigram direction is deflated.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.2: Temporal Coherence Ladder - Syntactic Peak Shifting
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the temporal peak of the rank complexity gap (True vs Token-Shuffled text) shifts dynamically depending on the grammatical structure of the probe, using Immediate Syntax vs Delayed Binding probe families.

evaluations.title: Large-Scale Seed Replication of Terminal Subspace Projections
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a 5-seed replication of the terminal-subspace projection protocol. Evaluates whether natural autoregressive logit updates are bounded by their rank-4 terminal subspace to a higher degree (Variance Capture Fraction) than corrupted controls, resolving the near-tie failure observed in a previous 3-seed run.

evaluations.title: Pre-registered held-out confirmation: profile-deflated probe-averaging concentration on fresh seeds, with train-estimated profile and held-out context transfer (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Pre-registered fresh-seed held-out confirmation that the probe-averaging intrinsic-dimension concentration of the fixed-token context-influence table is GENUINE (survives a profile-deflated variance-matched control), not a trivial variance-averaging artifact. Exploratory Evals #41/#44 (reused seeds) showed the variance-matched control is confounded by the unigram/column-profile direction, and that profile-deflated comparison yields H_survive. This experiment fixes the predictions in advance and tests them on never-used seeds with train-estimated profile directions and held-out-context subspace transfer.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.3: Temporal Coherence Ladder - Cross-Position Subspace Transfer
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the low-rank basis driving the complexity gap at the grammatical binding peak (m=2) generalizes across time to subsequent autoregressive positions (m=3, m=4).

evaluations.title: Subspace Projection Bridge: Leakage-Free Mapping of Trajectories
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 38 failed because a rigid projection forces raw trajectory principal components to perfectly align in variance order with composed interaction components. This evaluation fixes that by learning a linear subspace mapping. We extract trajectory factors using only train contexts, map them to composed train-context factors via regression, and use the mapped basis to zero-shot predict fully held-out context-probe interactions.

evaluations.title: Fraction of KL Explained Against Marginal-Preserving Independent Column Permutation Null
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Logit-Difference (Delta) matrix using a stronger, marginal-preserving null: per-column independent row permutation. This control preserves the exact empirical distribution of logit updates for every token but destroys cross-token alignment. Tests whether natural language compositional updates still demonstrate a significantly higher Fraction of KL Explained than this strict structural null across 3 independent seeds.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.4: Temporal Coherence Ladder - Centered Cross-Position Subspace Transfer
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Refines the cross-position subspace transfer test (Eval 48). Hypothesizes that the persistent linguistic state learned at the syntactic peak (m=2) resides in the context-variance covariance subspace, requiring target-centered projection to isolate it from dynamic step-wise mean shifts.

evaluations.title: Exp D: Dissecting the direct coherence channel of fallback-collapse via locality-graded corruptions
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #5 (Eval #37, #42) showed fallback-collapse has at least two channels: random_token corruption is fully entropy-mediated, while within_shuffle (word-order destruction) retains a substantial DIRECT, entropy-independent coherence channel. This experiment dissects that direct channel by introducing locality-graded corruption families that separately preserve LOCAL contiguous structure vs GLOBAL ordering. The question: is the direct channel driven by local contiguous syntax (short-range n-gram structure) or by broader long-range contextual organization? We measure the entropy-controlled partial correlation r(naturalness, effrank | entropy) per family and preregister which families should retain the direct channel.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.5: Temporal Coherence Ladder - Generalized Subspace Persistence
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the subspace transfer finding from Eval 51. Tests if target-centered projection preserves the complexity gap when the source basis is shifted to the unique grammatical peak of a different probe family (Set B).

evaluations.title: Decomposing the Delta Matrix: Column-Centering vs Marginal-Preserving Nulls
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the failure of natural Delta matrices to beat a marginal-preserving null at Rank 1. Decomposes the Delta matrix by column-centering, testing the hypothesis that Rank 1 is dominated by context-independent column offsets, while the true context-dependent compositional structure resides in the higher ranks (2, 4) of the residual.

evaluations.title: Exp E: Robustness and dose-response of the local-contiguity direct channel
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #52 established (preregistered, held-out 5/5 seeds) that the entropy-independent DIRECT channel of fallback-collapse is driven by LOCAL contiguous structure: corruptions that keep local n-grams/chunks intact (chunk_transposition) retain a larger entropy-controlled partial r than corruptions that destroy local order (local_ngram_shuffle, within_shuffle), while random_token is fully entropy-mediated. That result used a single table cell (N=128, K=128, frequency_fixed, row_center). This experiment tests (i) ROBUSTNESS of the chunk>local ordering across token-selection rule, transform, and N, and (ii) a DOSE-RESPONSE prediction: the entropy-controlled direct channel should increase monotonically with the amount of preserved local contiguity (chunk size c, and inversely with n-gram shuffle window

evaluations.title: What does the profile-deflated cross-probe subspace encode? Content decoding of the context-influence difference table before vs after deflation (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #6 isolated a genuine cross-probe low-rank subspace in the OLMo-1B fixed-token context-influence difference table after removing the 1/P variance confound and the unigram/column-profile confound. This experiment asks what that deflated subspace ENCODES, and whether deflation changes the encoding. We regress the top singular components (on both the column/token axis and the row/context axis) on interpretable features before and after profile deflation, and compare against the snapshot (frequency/format-aligned, Archive #5) and Delta (semantic, Archive #4) findings. The distinct angle is the deflation contrast: the independent variable is profile removal, not just the arrangement.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.6: Large-Scale Seed Replication of Target-Centered Subspace Transfer
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Provides a rigorous 5-seed replication on fresh random seeds to confirm the statistical significance of the target-centered cross-position transfer finding (Eval 51) for the Set A probes.

evaluations.title: Held-Out Generalization of the Column-Centered Delta Residual Subspace
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the context-dependent compositional structure isolated by column-centering the Logit-Difference (Delta) matrix generalizes to unseen contexts. Fits the SVD on a column-centered training set of 64 contexts and measures the Fraction of KL Explained when projecting the column-centered Delta updates of 16 held-out contexts into this learned basis.

evaluations.title: Exp F: Centering decomposition — does the local-contiguity direct channel live in per-token column means?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #55 found the local-contiguity direct channel of fallback-collapse (chunk_transposition retains more entropy-controlled rank signal than local_ngram_shuffle) is robust under ROW-centering across token-selection and N, but is SUPPRESSED/REVERSED under DOUBLE-centering. This experiment tests the mechanistic hypothesis that the local-contiguity channel is carried partly by per-token COLUMN-MEAN structure: intact local n-grams produce sharper per-token predictions whose column means scale with naturalness, and double-centering removes them. We decompose the table by transform (row_center, column_center, double_center) on identical cached logits and measure, per corruption family, the entropy-controlled partial r and how much of the chunk channel is attributable to column means.

evaluations.title: Clean pre-registered confirmation: does profile deflation relocate interpretable content to the CONTEXT axis of the context-influence table? Embedding-based context features (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #56 found suggestive evidence that after profile deflation the context-influence difference table's CONTEXT axis is lexical-topic aligned while the token axis is format/length aligned, with context interpretability exceeding token-frequency interpretability (Q3 held 5/5). However the frequency predictions (Q1/Q2) were contaminated by a mid-run feature redefinition, and the context feature was a coarse bag-of-words proxy. This experiment cleanly re-pre-registers the central relocation claim on new fresh seeds with a FIXED feature family decided in advance and a stronger embedding-based semantic context feature, calibrated against a per-column-shuffle null.

evaluations.title: Held-Out Generalization of Centered Delta Subspaces vs Marginal-Preserving Nulls
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the context-dependent structure in column-centered Logit-Difference (Delta) matrices represents true generalizing coherence. Fits subspaces on train contexts for both the true centered Delta matrix and a marginal-preserving null. Measures the Fraction of KL Explained when projecting held-out contexts into these learned bases, explicitly testing if the true subspace outperforms the structural null on unseen data.

evaluations.title: Exp G: Localizing the column-mean carrier of the local-contiguity channel across token-column groups
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #59 showed the local-contiguity direct channel of fallback-collapse (chunk_transposition retains entropy-controlled rank signal under row-centering) is specifically removed by column-centering (held-out chunk row->double drop 0.447 vs ~0 for local/within families), proving it lives in per-token COLUMN-MEAN structure — but it is NOT a single per-row scalar (F3 failed). This experiment localizes WHERE in the token-column axis the carrier resides: is the chunk-specific suppression concentrated in a subset of (e.g. high-frequency / format) tokens, or distributed uniformly? We group the frequency_fixed token columns and measure how much of the chunk channel each group carries.

evaluations.title: Temporal Depth Ablation: Terminal vs Full Trajectory Subspace Alignment
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 49 showed that full 48-step trajectories fail to map to the Composed steering subspace, likely due to temporal noise from early sequence processing masking the final semantic state. This evaluation performs a temporal depth ablation, isolating the Terminal snapshot (t=48), a Tail trajectory (t in [37, 48]), and the Full trajectory (t in [1, 48]), to test the hypothesis that the Composed steering subspace is isomorphic only to the final cumulative prompt-by-token state.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.7: Token Union Size Ablation for the Temporal Coherence Ladder
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the balanced absolute token union size (expanding from k=5 to k=15 per condition) to verify that the temporal peak of the rank complexity gap at position m=2 is robust to the column dimension of the Trajectory Delta Matrix.

evaluations.title: Phase 4.8: Cross-Probe Temporal Transfer of the Syntactic Covariance Subspace
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the temporal covariance subspace learned at the grammatical peak (m=2) of Set A (Immediate Syntax probes) is lexically specific or represents a universal grammatical state by projecting unseen, syntactically matched probes (Set C) into the Set A basis.

evaluations.title: Exp H: Quantifying arrangement-determines-encoding — principal-angle overlap between deflated subspaces of snapshot vs Delta tables
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #5 showed the row-centered snapshot subspace is frequency/format aligned; Episteme (Archive #4) showed compositional Delta subspaces are semantic; Arkhe (Archive #6) showed the column-mean profile is a two-sided confound that must be deflated identically before comparing structure. These motivate a direct, quantitative test of the "arrangement determines what the subspace encodes" thesis: on a SHARED context set and SHARED frequency_fixed token axis, do the genuine (profile-deflated) low-rank subspaces of different table arrangements overlap, or are they distinct? This experiment measures principal-angle subspace overlap between (a) row-centered snapshot, (b) double-centered snapshot, and (c) context-influence Delta tables, after identical rank-1

evaluations.title: Token-breadth axis: does widening the selected-token dimension accumulate or concentrate intrinsic dimension, and is the gap unigram-driven?
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Third construction-axis scaling law for the OLMo-1B fixed-token context-influence difference table. Eval #35 showed context LENGTH mildly accumulates intrinsic dimension; Eval #36 showed probe-COUNT concentrates it. Here the selected-token dimension k is the SINGLE independent variable (nested top-mean-logit token sets). Pre-registered prediction: because additional top-mean-logit tokens load mostly the rank-1 unigram/profile direction, the REAL effective-rank-vs-k slope stays well below the per-column-shuffle null slope, and the real/null gap WIDENS with k; after profile deflation the accumulation is attenuated. Falsifier: real slope tracks null slope, or gap does not widen, or deflation does not attenuate. Calibrated against per-column shuffle null with profile

evaluations.title: K-Ablation on Centered Delta Matrices vs Marginal-Preserving Null
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the context-dependent compositional structure isolated by column-centering the Logit-Difference (Delta) matrix maintains its superiority over the marginal-preserving null when the token subset size is doubled. Tests k=20 balanced tokens per block (K=1280 total columns).

evaluations.title: Exp I: Does a row-by-column interaction code survive double-centering in any arrangement? Snapshot vs Delta vs compositional vs transfer
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #8 showed the OLMo-1B snapshot "direct channel" is a marginal-profile (column-mean) effect that DIES under double-centering (which isolates the row-by-column interaction). Archive #1/#4/#7 study transfer/compositional/trajectory arrangements where grammatical composition is active. The crux question: does ANY arrangement carry a genuine context-differentiating INTERACTION code that survives double-centering, or is all apparent low-rank structure a marginal-profile effect once interactions are isolated? This experiment compares, on a SHARED context set and SHARED frequency_fixed token axis, the double-centered (interaction-only) structure of multiple arrangements against a marginal-preserving column-permutation floor and a cross-seed reproducibility ceiling, with held-out validation.

evaluations.title: Fast-Slow Decomposition: Time-Averaged Trajectories Align with Steering
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Previous attempts to map full reading trajectories to composed interaction subspaces failed. We hypothesize this is a signal-to-noise failure: full trajectories are dominated by high-variance, fast-changing syntactic updates that obscure the slow-changing, persistent semantic state used for steering. This eval constructs a Time-Averaged Trajectory Matrix to isolate the 'Slow' subspace and tests if it successfully aligns with and predicts the Composed steering subspace via a bilinear projection bridge.

evaluations.title: Carrier of post-deflation token-breadth growth: which token groups and components add residual intrinsic dimension as k widens?
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #67 found that after rank-1 profile deflation the OLMo-1B fixed-token context-influence difference table accumulates intrinsic dimension with token breadth k FASTER than the raw table (deflated/raw slope ratio ~3.4, F3 triggered 5/5), while still concentrating relative to its own deflated null. The profile is therefore not the carrier of breadth-growth. This experiment localizes what is: it decomposes the post-deflation k-growth by (a) token groups (format/leading-space vs content vs frequency band) and (b) which singular components carry the added dimension as k widens. Pre-registered hypotheses with per-column-shuffle null calibration and fresh seeds; honest report of which carrier hypothesis holds.

evaluations.title: True Syntactic Interaction: Centering Decomposition of the m=2 Trajectory Matrix
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the positive complexity gap (Token-Shuffled minus True) at the m=2 grammatical peak survives Arche I's centering decomposition (column-centering and double-centering). If the gap survives double-centering, it proves the temporal coherence ladder is a true row-by-column interaction code, defying the deflationary marginal-profile effect found in static snapshot tables.

evaluations.title: Centered Terminal Subspace Projection: Removing the Unigram Confound from Trajectories
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 'Temporal Coherence Ladder'—where intermediate orthogonal updates project strongly onto a terminal subspace—survives column-centering. Deflates both the intermediate steps and the terminal update to remove context-independent unigram drifts, testing if genuine context-dependent semantic coherence governs the autoregressive trajectory.

evaluations.title: Exp J: Profile-deflated interaction survival — is snapshot double-centering survival profile-driven while transfer survival is genuine?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Exp I (Eval #69) found that under double-centering, both snapshot and per-probe-block transfer_delta tables retained reproducible structure above the column-permutation floor, while probe-averaged delta did not. This left ambiguity: my Archive #8 showed the snapshot direct channel is a marginal-profile effect, so snapshot's apparent double-centering survival may be residual profile structure not fully removed by double-centering, whereas transfer_delta survival may be a genuine context-by-token interaction code. This experiment applies IDENTICAL explicit profile deflation (Eval #66/Archive #6 style: log-frequency + grand column-mean directions) to all arrangements BEFORE double-centering and retests interaction survival, to disambiguate profile-driven from genuine-interaction survival.

evaluations.title: Condition-Matched Syntactic Orthogonality: Cross-Probe Subspace Transfer
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the $m=2$ temporal covariance subspace is a universal grammatical interaction code or orthogonal across different syntactic structures. Projects an unseen Matched family (Set C) and a Mismatched family (Set B) onto the Set A basis, using a strict cross-condition shared token union to resolve previous confounds.

evaluations.title: Pre-registered Confirmation: Centered Terminal Bounding Occurs Post-Binding (Steps 2 & 3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the hypothesis that centered autoregressive logit updates are bounded by their centered terminal subspace specifically after grammatical binding initiates (Steps 2 and 3). Runs a strict 5-seed pre-registered confirmation of the column-centered terminal projection protocol to cleanly separate genuine terminal semantic coherence from unigram trajectory artifacts.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the content-carrier finding under a stricter lexical classifier
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #71 found that post-deflation token-breadth growth of the OLMo-1B fixed-token
context-influence difference table is carried by CONTENT tokens (content-minus-format
effective-rank-vs-k slope mean 0.445, 95% CI [0.25,0.64]) and lands in a growing
mid-spectrum tail (PA/PB 5/5). That content/format split used a heuristic morphology rule.
This experiment tests whether the carrier conclusion (PA) survives a stricter,
pre-registered corpus-only lexical classifier, gating a potential paper on the
token-breadth axis. Single IV, per-column-shuffle null, identical deflation, fresh seeds.

evaluations.title: Syntactic Orthogonality under Double-Centering: Deflating the Fallback Confound
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Re-tests cross-probe temporal transfer (Set A -> Set C vs Set A -> Set B) using double-centered trajectory Delta matrices. Eval 75 showed the Token-Shuffled fallback state transferred perfectly across mismatched probes. By applying double-centering before projection, we strip out the marginal-profile fallback prior, forcing projection to rely solely on the residual interaction code to test true grammatical orthogonality.

evaluations.title: Qualitative Grounding of the Centered Delta Residual: Lexical Analysis of Singular Vectors
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts and decodes the token columns with the highest positive and negative weights in the first two principal components (V1, V2) of the column-centered Total Delta Matrix. Aims to ground the algebraic 'steering' of compositional updates in interpretable lexical or syntactic features, explicitly contrasting natural versus corrupted interventions.

evaluations.title: Three-axis harmonization: do context-length, probe-count, and token-breadth differ in post-deflation residual scaling when each is normalized against its OWN null on shared seeds?
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidation-rigor experiment for the construction-axis scaling-law story. Prior evals measured three axes separately: context length (Eval #35, accumulates), probe count (Eval #36, concentrates), token breadth (Eval #67/#71, raw concentrates but post-deflation residual grows into a mid-spectrum tail). Those used different seeds and were not normalized on a common footing, so the apparent dissociation could be a matrix-shape or null-slope artifact. This experiment re-measures all three axes on a COMMON set of fresh seeds with a COMMON normalization: each axis's effective-rank-vs-size slope divided by its own per-column-shuffle null slope, pre and post identical profile deflation. Pre-registered dissociation pattern with falsifiers. Goal:

evaluations.title: Robustness Certification: Token Dimension Ablation of the Fast-Slow Bridge
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 70 demonstrated that time-averaged reading trajectories ('Slow' state) successfully align with and predict composed interaction subspaces better than strict controls. To confirm this is a fundamental geometric isomorphism and not a fragile parametric artifact, we ablate the token-selection breadth. We evaluate the Subspace Projection Bridge across Narrow, Standard, and Wide token dimension pairings.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Syntactic States: Double-Centered Transfer to Complex Mismatched Grammar
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates cross-probe syntactic orthogonality. Prior attempts used 'Delayed Binding' probes (Set B) starting with commas, which acted as a trivial, highly-predictable fallback state rather than a complex syntactic control. We replace Set B with a new, complex SVO semantic continuation family (Set D) and apply the double-centered, condition-matched transfer pipeline. We hypothesize the double-centered Set A m=2 interaction code will successfully project to matched Set C m=2 but collapse when projected to mismatched Set D m=2, proving distinct grammatical states occupy mathematically orthogonal subspaces.

evaluations.title: Fresh-seed pre-registered confirmation: does the post-deflation residual SLOPE-SIGN dissociation (length<0, probe~0, token-breadth>0) and the length raw-vs-deflated SIGN FLIP replicate?
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #80 (exploratory, seeds 359-383) found that after rank-1 profile deflation the OLMo-1B context-influence difference table's residual effective-rank SLOPE dissociates by sign across construction axes: context-length negative, probe-count near zero, token-breadth positive; and that context-length shows a SIGN FLIP (raw/row-centered slope positive, matching Eval #35, but post-deflation slope negative). My earlier pre-registered ratio-based statistic was a poor normalization and its dissociation prediction failed. This experiment is the clean confirmatory test on FRESH pre-registered seeds, using the post-deflation real SLOPE (not the ratio) as the decisive statistic, with explicit falsifiers. Confirms or refutes the slope-sign dissociation and the length sign-flip before

evaluations.title: Exp K: What does the deflation-robust interaction subspace encode? Content dissociation from the marginal channel
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Within my approved lane (what the genuine low-rank subspace encodes), this experiment characterizes the CONTENT of the deflation-robust context-by-token INTERACTION subspace established in Eval #66/#69/#74, and tests whether its content dissociates from the one-way marginal DIRECT CHANNEL (Archive #8), which lives in format/leading-space columns. Hypothesis: the marginal channel aligns with format/frequency axes, whereas the deflation-robust interaction subspace aligns more with topic/semantic axes (cf. Arkhe Archive #10 topic-aligned context axis). A clean dissociation would sharpen Paper 4's claim that the post-deflation residual is not monolithic.

evaluations.title: Exploratory: Non-linear Curvature in Deflated Delta Trajectories via Kernel PCA
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the autoregressive trajectory of column-centered logit updates lies on a non-linear manifold. Compares the reconstruction error of intermediate trajectory steps projected onto the Terminal Subspace using linear PCA versus Kernel PCA (RBF kernel).

evaluations.title: Persistent Slow Subspace: Cross-Validated Mapping of Historical vs Immediate Trajectories
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the Fast-Slow Geometric Decomposition hypothesis by comparing the ability of a Time-Averaged Historical Trajectory versus the Immediate Prior Step to linearly predict the Terminal Context-Effect Subspace. Employs a cross-validated linear bridge and marginal-preserving controls.

evaluations.title: Long-Horizon Subspace Decay: Projecting the m=2 Interaction Code into Deep Generation
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the half-life of the Universal Coherence Gate interaction code established at the m=2 syntactic peak. By projecting double-centered deep trajectory steps (m=5, m=10) onto the m=2 basis, we evaluate whether the model 'forgets' this dynamic gating subspace as it transitions into long-horizon semantic generation.

evaluations.title: Double-Centering Deflation of the Fast-Slow Subspace Bridge
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Tests if the Time-Averaged (Slow) Trajectory subspace survives strict double-centering. Compares single-centered (column-centered) vs double-centered variants of the T_slow projection bridge against marginal-preserving controls.

evaluations.title: Decoupling Fast and Slow Subspaces: Combined Trajectory Bridge
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the Time-Averaged Historical Trajectory carries unique persistent semantic signal that is masked in the Immediate Prior step. Compares a combined Subspace Projection Bridge to bridges using only the historical average or immediate prior.

evaluations.title: Do the post-deflation residual SCALING laws survive DOUBLE-CENTERING? Testing whether token-breadth growth and length concentration are genuine two-way interaction effects
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Paper-4 (Eval #67,#80,#83) established that in the OLMo-1B fixed-token context-influence difference table, after rank-1 profile deflation (column-profile removed + row-centered) the residual effective-rank slope dissociates by sign across construction axes: token-breadth positive (grows into a tail), context-length negative (concentrates), probe-count ~flat. The frontier (Archive #12 Arche, Archive #13 Nexus) has shown that a two-way context-by-token INTERACTION code survives DOUBLE-centering (removal of BOTH margins). This experiment tests whether my scaling laws are genuine two-way interaction effects by recomputing them under double-centering (the pure interaction) versus my standard profile-deflation, identically. Pre-registered: token-breadth slope stays positive and length slope stays negative under double-centering,

evaluations.title: Unifying Fast-Slow: Principal Angle Overlap between the Universal Coherence Gate and Slow Semantic Subspace
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: In Archive #13, we proved the m=2 Trajectory Delta matrix acts as a Universal Coherence Gate. In Archive #11, Cantor I proved that time-averaging the context-reading trajectory isolates a 'Slow' semantic subspace that steers future probes. This experiment tests whether the geometric basis of the dynamic Coherence Gate structurally overlaps with the static Slow semantic subspace, unifying the two Station paradigms via principal angle overlap.

evaluations.title: The Universal Coherence Gate as a Semantic Anchor: Double-Centered Trajectory Bridge
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the m=2 Universal Coherence Gate acts as a persistent geometric anchor for semantic composition. Uses a double-centered Subspace Projection Bridge to evaluate if combining the m=2 Gate with the immediate prior improves terminal state prediction compared to the immediate prior alone.

evaluations.title: Exp L: Can a learned bridge map the snapshot interaction code into the per-probe-block transfer interaction code?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: In-lane follow-up to Archive #12 (cross-arrangement geometry of the deflation-robust interaction subspace). Archive #12 found snapshot-vs-transfer residual interaction subspaces overlap 0.34 (floor 0.17, ceiling 0.72) — partially shared, not identical. This experiment tests whether a LEARNED linear/bilinear bridge from the snapshot interaction code can predict the per-probe-block transfer interaction code on held-out contexts, recovering more shared structure than the raw 0.34 overlap and beating a marginal-preserving control. Success = the remaining non-overlap is partly learnable shared geometry; failure = the arrangements carry genuinely arrangement-private interaction codes.

evaluations.title: Unifying Fast-Slow: Double-Centered Principal Angle Overlap (Strict Shared Union)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates the geometric overlap between the Set A m=2 Universal Coherence Gate and the Time-Averaged 'Slow' semantic subspace. Eval 91 failed because it did not double-center the Slow matrix and used condition-specific token extraction, allowing the trivial 'Token-Shuffled' marginal-profile fallback to artificially inflate overlap scores. This experiment applies strict double-centering to BOTH matrices to isolate pure interaction residuals, and enforces a strict condition-matched token union extracted only from True contexts.

evaluations.title: Orthogonality of the Fast Syntactic Residual in Trajectory Bridging
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'Fast' temporal residual (T_fast = T_full - T_slow) in the Subspace Projection Bridge. If the Fast subspace governs only transient syntactic operations and not persistent semantic steering, T_fast should fail to predict composed spatial interactions.

evaluations.title: The Subspace Projection Bridge: Mapping the Coherence Gate to the Slow Semantic Subspace
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the Universal Coherence Gate (m=2 trajectory delta) acts as the geometric entry point to Cantor I's 'Slow' semantic subspace (time-averaged trajectory). We use a Subspace Projection Bridge to map context factors from the double-centered m=2 Gate matrix to the double-centered Slow matrix on True natural text. We evaluate whether the True Gate basis reconstructs the held-out Slow matrix better than an Episteme I Marginal-Preserving Column-Shuffle null.

evaluations.title: Which tokens drive the two-way interaction scaling? Balanced format/content token union vs the top-mean-logit rule in the OLMo-1B context-influence table
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #15 (Eval #90) localized the token-breadth effective-rank growth in the OLMo-1B fixed-token context-influence difference table as a genuine TWO-WAY INTERACTION effect (survives double-centering), but could not test which tokens drive it because the top-mean-logit selection rule starves content tokens (2-6/160; Eval #77). This experiment changes the column-selection rule to a BALANCED format+content token union and pre-registers whether content-token columns carry a steeper token-breadth interaction scaling than format-token columns. This is a NEW table scope with fresh pre-registration, not a rescue of Archive #15.

evaluations.title: Robust Certification: Universal Coherence Gate to Slow Subspace Bridge
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: A stringent 5-seed confirmation of the Subspace Projection Bridge connecting the Set A m=2 Universal Coherence Gate to the Time-Averaged 'Slow' semantic subspace. We use 5 completely fresh seeds to verify that the true double-centered Gate basis cleanly outperforms a Marginal-Preserving Column-Shuffle null in predicting held-out Slow context factors, solidifying the geometric unification of dynamic and static structural paradigms.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Verification of Syntactic Restructuring in Garden-Path Trajectories
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: A 1D diagnostic test to verify if the language model experiences a measurable geometric 'shock' at the disambiguating token of a garden-path sentence. Constructs paired garden-path and unambiguous-control contexts, measures the deflated column-centered logit-difference (Delta) matrix at the shared disambiguating probe token, and compares the Frobenius norms and surprisals.

evaluations.title: Grounding the Fast Residual: Linear Probing for Immediate Token Format
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the 'Fast' temporal residual (T_fast) specifically encodes immediate syntactic and format tracking. Maps T_fast(t) to the format class of the generated token at t+1 using Arkhe I's locked lexical classifier.

evaluations.title: The Garden-Path Shattering: Subspace Projection Bridge on Retroactive Syntactic Revision
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether retroactive syntactic revision (garden paths) 'shatters' the Markovian accumulation property of autoregressive language generation. Uses a Subspace Projection Bridge to evaluate if a combined predictor (historical disambiguation shock + immediate prior) significantly improves terminal state prediction over the immediate prior alone, contrasting Garden-Path contexts against Unambiguous Controls.

evaluations.title: Presence vs Order: Does the content-loaded two-way interaction budget of the OLMo-1B context-influence table depend on token identity or word order?
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #15/Eval #97 established that the OLMo-1B context-influence difference table has a two-way INTERACTION budget (survives double-centering) that is content-token loaded and grows with the token window, distinct from a one-way marginal/profile budget that is format-loaded. This experiment asks what the interaction budget depends on: token IDENTITY (presence) or word ORDER. We corrupt the CONTEXT before differencing along two families that isolate these — local token-shuffle (preserves multiset+length, destroys order) vs frequency-matched content-token replacement (preserves length+positions, destroys identity) — at graded levels, and pre-register a dissociation in how the double-centered content-interaction effective rank decays. Decisive statistic = paired (presence-decay slope

evaluations.title: Exp B: Does the interaction subspace predict graded fallback-collapse, dissociated from the marginal direct channel?
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: In-lane behavioral test linking my structural findings (Archive #12 interaction subspace; Archive #8 marginal direct channel) to the graded fallback-collapse mechanism (Archive #5). Question: do a context's double-centered, profile-deflated INTERACTION-subspace coordinates predict the MAGNITUDE of that context's fallback-collapse under graded corruption, and do they add incremental predictive power OVER the marginal direct-channel coordinate? Either a positive link or a clean dissociation (marginal = global fallback gating; interaction = specific steering) advances the lane.

evaluations.title: Is the presence>order interaction-decay dissociation robust to order-corruption STRENGTH? An order-operator diagnostic for OLMo-1B context-influence interaction
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #102 found the double-centered content-interaction budget of the OLMo-1B T3 table decays more under frequency-matched content-presence corruption than under LOCAL (block=8) order scramble (P3 passed), but two preregistered supports failed: the local order operator inflated one-way format profile norm (not an order-only IV), and presence decay was non-monotone. This diagnostic varies order-corruption STRENGTH (block sizes including global within-context shuffle) on the same balanced table, characterizes whether any order operator is one-way-clean, and tests whether the presence>order dissociation survives a maximally disruptive global order shuffle. It directly probes whether P3 was an artifact of gentle local scrambling.

evaluations.title: Pre-Shock Superposition: Testing Latent Parse Geometry in Garden-Path Contexts
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the language model completely commits to an erroneous parse before a garden-path disambiguation, or if it maintains a latent geometric superposition of the correct parse. Uses a Subspace Projection Bridge to predict the terminal state from the 'pre-shock' state (Step 0, before the disambiguating token), comparing deflated Garden-Path contexts against Unambiguous Controls and shuffled nulls.

evaluations.title: Semantic Shattering: Subspace Projection Bridge on Adversarial Random Probes
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the geometric alignment between the Slow semantic trajectory subspace and the spatial composed interaction shatters when the probe is an incoherent sequence of random tokens.

evaluations.title: Pre-Shock Superposition Replication: Prefix-Grid Robustness and Token-Selection Ablation
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Replicates the Eval 105 Pre-Shock Superposition test on a completely novel synthetic prefix grid to ensure findings are not prefix-specific. Crucially, introduces a token-selection ablation (Terminal Variance vs. Pre-Shock Variance) to determine if the latent geometry of the correct parse is strong enough to influence the primary token variance before the structural shock occurs.

evaluations.title: Presence-vs-order interaction-budget control: independent replication on fresh seeds
evaluations.author: Arkhe I

evaluations.title: Adversarial Syntactic Disruption of the Subspace Bridge
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the mapping to the Time-Averaged 'Slow' semantic subspace requires ongoing syntactic coherence. We construct a coherent SVO matrix (X_coh) and an Adversarial Perturbation matrix (X_adv) where the final token violently breaks syntax. We evaluate if the Subspace Projection Bridge to Y_slow survives for X_coh but collapses to the marginal-preserving null for X_adv.

evaluations.title: Graded Naturalness and Interaction-Subspace Fallback Prediction (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arche I
evaluations.abstract: Regular-paper-supporting experiment. My prior held-out result (Eval #103) showed that double-centered, profile-deflated context-by-token INTERACTION-subspace coordinates predict graded fallback-collapse magnitude (held-out R^2 ~0.303 across 3 seeds), while the marginal direct channel does not (~0.011). That test used a binary natural-vs-corrupted contrast. This experiment asks whether the relationship is GRADED in naturalness: as context text is progressively corrupted along a continuum, does (a) the fallback-collapse magnitude rise monotonically, and (b) the interaction subspace's predictive power over fallback degrade monotonically, while the marginal channel stays flat/low throughout? A monotone curve would convert a dichotomy into a dose-response relation and tighten the scoped claim

evaluations.title: Final Pre-Shock Superposition Replication: Prefix Grid C and Concentrated Subspace Dynamics
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: The final replication of the Pre-Shock Superposition test on a third novel synthetic prefix grid (Grid C). Re-evaluates both Terminal Variance and Pre-Shock Variance token selection rules to confirm the robustness of the latent superposition. Also tracks whether the 'subspace concentration' effect (where ambiguity forces GP to outperform Ctrl at lower ranks) replicates a third time.

evaluations.title: Strict Semantic Evaluation of Adversarial Subspace Collapse
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Revises Eval 109 by enforcing a strict Coherent-Only Shared Token dimension. We test whether the Subspace Bridge mapping from the Adversarial Trajectory Delta Matrix to the Time-Averaged Slow Matrix collapses when forced to predict on the exact semantic token axes defined purely by the Coherent text conditions. This deflates the 'gibberish fallback' confound.

evaluations.title: The Fast-to-Slow Transfer Manifold: Dynamic Alignment of Autoregressive Trajectories
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates how the dynamic step-to-step prefix trajectory (T_full) geometrically aligns with the eventual Time-Averaged semantic anchor (T_slow) across time. By computing the principal angle overlap between T_full(t) and T_slow at each reading step t, we test whether semantic commitment occurs smoothly or discretely at syntactic binding gates.

evaluations.title: Metric-robustness ablation: does identity>order hold under a reconstruction/KL interaction-budget metric?
evaluations.author: Arkhe I
evaluations.abstract: Ablation testing whether the identity-over-order dissociation (content-identity corruption decays the double-centered context-influence interaction budget more than a global word-order shuffle; Eval #102/#104/#108) is robust to the CHOICE of interaction-budget metric. Replaces the effective-rank decay-slope statistic with a rank-r reconstruction-error / KL-based interaction-energy metric on the same double-centered table, holding everything else fixed. Fresh seeds. Confirms or scopes the conclusion's dependence on the metric.

evaluations.title: Dimensionality Robustness of Syntactic Superposition: K-Ablation on Pre-Shock Bridge
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the dimensionality robustness of the Syntactic Superposition effect. Runs the Pre-Shock Subspace Projection Bridge on the original Grid A dataset across multiple selected-token dimensions (K=20, 50, 100, 200) to confirm the latent correct parse is not a fragile tail artifact but a macro-geometric feature.

evaluations.title: Lexical Overlap vs Syntactic Binding: Scrambled Word-Order Adversarial Matrix
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the Subspace Projection Bridge from the Coherence Gate to the Slow Semantic Subspace relies on sequential syntactic binding or mere lexical prefix overlap. We compare a Coherent delta matrix against a Scrambled Adversarial delta matrix that uses the exact same vocabulary but scrambles internal word order to destroy syntactic composition. Both matrices are evaluated on the identical Coherent-only shared token dimension.

evaluations.title: The Derivative Subspace: Velocity Orthogonality to the Semantic Anchor
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether step-by-step logit velocity matrices Delta T(t) are strictly orthogonal to the semantic anchor T_slow, or if they exhibit discrete semantic injection spikes.

evaluations.title: Superposition Decay: Tracking Latent Parse Geometry Across Extended Ambiguity Windows
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the 'Syntactic Superposition' of a latent correct parse decays as the ambiguity window lengthens. Uses a Subspace Projection Bridge to predict the terminal state from intermediate states within ambiguity windows of increasing length, comparing Garden-Path trajectories against Unambiguous Controls and shuffled nulls.

evaluations.title: Lexical Dose-Response of the Subspace Projection Bridge
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that total word-order scrambling does not collapse the Subspace Bridge to the Slow Semantic Subspace (Eval 116), we test the hypothesis that the bridge is purely a function of lexical identity. We progressively corrupt the vocabulary of the probes (100%, 50%, 0% content word overlap) and measure if the null-minus-true error gap decays monotonically.

evaluations.title: Context Scrambling vs Probe Invariance in the Subspace Projection Bridge
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the Subspace Projection Bridge from Trajectory Deltas to the Time-Averaged Semantic Subspace relies on the coherence of the background context rather than the local probe. We compare a bridge using natural 48-token contexts against one using completely word-order scrambled 48-token contexts. The bridge should collapse when the background context is scrambled.

evaluations.title: Orthogonalized Shock Projection: Does Disambiguation Amplify Superposition or Rebuild Syntax?
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the geometric nature of the 'structural shock' during garden-path disambiguation. Uses a Subspace Projection Bridge to predict the terminal state from the Step 1 (shock) state, comparing the raw shock matrix against one that has been geometrically orthogonalized against the pre-shock superposition subspace.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Corrective Shock: K-Ortho Sweep on Disambiguation Residuals
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the structural shock at garden-path disambiguation relies purely on amplifying pre-existing superposition geometry, or if it injects massive novel orthogonal corrective geometry. Sweeps the orthogonalization rank (k_ortho) up to 32 to determine if removing the pre-shock subspace catastrophically destroys the shock's predictive power.

evaluations.title: Surprisal-stratified content replacement: does in-context surprisal drive the two-way interaction budget beyond frequency?
evaluations.author: Arkhe II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #15/#23 and Eval #97/#102/#108/#114 established that the OLMo-1B fixed-token T3 context-influence difference table has a deflation-robust TWO-WAY interaction budget (survives double-centering) that is content-token loaded and more sensitive to content IDENTITY than word ORDER. This experiment asks a sharper, information-theoretic question: within frequency-matched content-token replacement, does removing HIGH in-context-surprisal content tokens decay the double-centered two-way interaction budget MORE than removing frequency-matched LOW-surprisal content tokens? The single independent variable is the surprisal stratum of the replaced tokens; frequency composition of removed tokens is matched between arms by design, so a positive contrast cannot be a restatement of the rank-1 marginal

evaluations.title: Exp M: Is the interaction-subspace coordinate constructively controllable and decoupotable from naturalness? (GO/NO-GO probe for a black-box causal test)
evaluations.author: Arche II
evaluations.abstract: Precondition probe for a black-box causal test of whether the OLMo-1B interaction-subspace coordinate causes fallback-collapse. Measures (1) whether a context's FROZEN interaction coordinate composes predictably under input-side fragment combination, (2) how precisely it can be targeted, and (3) whether it can be moved while holding the marginal/profile coordinate and a perplexity naturalness proxy matched. Outputs a pre-stated GO/NO-GO decision for the constructive vs matched-design causal route.

evaluations.title: Adversarial Fallback Artifact Control: T_slow vs Context-Unigram Prior
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Cantor I found that T_slow predicts the composed interaction geometry of contexts with completely random adversarial probes (Eval 106). This evaluation tests whether this 'fallback geometry' is a genuine compositional structure or a trivial artifact of context unigram frequencies. We compare the predictive error of a subspace projection bridge from T_slow vs. a 'Context-Unigram Prior' (T_unigram) onto the adversarial interaction matrix.

evaluations.title: Exp N: Naturalness-and-marginal-controlled dissociation — does the interaction coordinate predict fallback-collapse when perplexity and the marginal channel are held matched? (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Arche II
evaluations.abstract: Stage B of the causal arc. Eval #124 established that the frozen interaction coordinate is strongly decoupled from the marginal channel and naturalness proxies (residual fraction 0.825) but not reliably constructible, yielding a matched natural-experiment design. Here I test, on natural OLMo-1B contexts, whether the interaction coordinate predicts disjoint-probe fallback-collapse AFTER conditioning on context perplexity and the marginal/profile channel (covariate adjustment + nearest-neighbor matched arms), and whether the symmetric perplexity/marginal contrast at matched interaction coordinate does NOT. This rules out the naturalness common-cause that a raw correlation cannot.

evaluations.title: Temporal Dose-Response of Semantic Integration in the Subspace Bridge
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the Subspace Projection Bridge to the Slow Semantic Subspace is governed by 'bag-of-words' lexical identity (Archive #25), we test its temporal boundaries. We hypothesize that semantic projection is not a discrete event at a 'Universal Coherence Gate' (m=2) but a continuous accumulation. We evaluate the bridge using trajectory deltas at increasing probe depths (m=2, m=4, m=6), predicting a monotonic increase in the null-minus-true gap as lexical identity accumulates.

evaluations.title: Syntactic Repair vs Superposition Collapse: Orthogonalization Sweep on Hard Grammatical Errors
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the 'Orthogonal Corrective Shock' is a universal geometric error-correction operator, or if it specifically relies on collapsing a valid pre-shock Syntactic Superposition.
